Event Name: On Location with Artichoke Dance | Robin Michals
Event Description: On Location with Artichoke Dance is a solo exhibition by Brooklyn-based photographer Robin Michals. Curated by Pam Wong, the exhibit showcases photographs of Artichoke Dance Company performing the Immersive Performance Tours of Gowanus conceived by Lynn Neuman in 2021, and co-hosted annually with various environmental and social justice organizations. The photographs on view feature Artichoke dancers moving through Gowanus in space and time and include images at the defunct Salt Lot in 2021 and the new 420 Carroll Street development in 2026. Michals merges the genres of dance photography and urban landscape photography in vibrant shots that capture the performances as well as the evolution of the neighborhood. The photos juxtapose the dancers as they work together to create patterns and shapes against a backdrop of the transforming waterfront. The photos offer an interpretation of the performances as a positive vision of urban life that values art, collaboration, and environmental awareness. In addition, there is a portrait of Neuman, in costume, on the tipping floor at SIMS Municipal Recycling, taken for Michals and Neuman’s collaborative project Waste Side Story. Michals and Neuman met in 2018 through a residency offered by Works on Water and Underwater New York on Governors Island. Michals, who had been working on environmental issues for 15 years, was struck by Lynn’s upcycling of plastic bags into costumes, and the pair began to work together to make images of a dancer wearing the costumes at locations that reflect the lifecycle of plastics from production to various end points including landfills and oceans. Several of these images were exhibited at The Old Stone House in 2021. Robin shifted her focus to dance photography after the pandemic, starting with her work with the Times Square Project in 2020 and 2021. For Robin, photographing the Artichoke Dance tours is an incredible opportunity to bring together her longstanding love of urban landscape photography and her much more recent, but no less profound, love of dance photography. —————- ON LOCATION WITH ARTICHOKE DANCE On view Saturdays: Sept 12, 19, 26 and Oct 3 from 1-5pm ON LOCATION WITH ARTICHOKE DANCE Programs: Sept. 12 (2:00–2:30pm): Video screening of Immersive Performance Tour Highlights: 2021–2026 with Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 12 (2:30-4:30pm): Join a guided tour using the Gowanus Augmented Reality Walking Tour App featuring animated virtual environments of the past as visual overlays on the canal-scape, as well as the Underground Waterways Soundwalk where voices from the past murmur and sing, led by Sarah Drury, Project Director. iPads and headphones provided, or download to your iPhone. The 20-minute tour will be available from 2:30-4:30pm. Sept. 19 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 26 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 26 (2:30pm): Role of the Arts in Change Making: A Conversation with Naturally Occurring Cultural Districts of New York Oct. 3 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company —————- About the Artist: Robin Michals is a photographer who specializes in dance and performance. She is completely omnivorous when it comes to dance with an interest in all forms from folkloric to street dance. Her clients include the international Human Rights Arts Festival and the Queensboro Dance Festival among many others. In 2025, she had a public installation of photos of dancers at the party Vinyl Nights in Albee Square in Downtown Brooklyn, sponsored by Downtown Brooklyn Partnership. Her work has also been in numerous publications including Hyperallergic, Queens Chronicle, and Time Out. Before shifting her focus to performance, she spent 15 years documenting environment issues including climate change and the fossil fuel industries. She was raised in Manhattan and moved to Brooklyn in the last century. Robin has taught photography at City Tech, CUNY, where her students are from all over the world, for 23 years. For more info: www.robinmichals.com About Artichoke Dance: Artichoke Dance Company, based in Brooklyn, NY, is known for innovative and engaging performances paired with environmental activism, education, community building and civic engagement. Previous large-scale projects have addressed plastic pollution mitigation on Coney Island, single use plastic bags in New York, sea level rise and climate migration, the remediation of the Gowanus Canal, river revitalization in Los Angeles, and water use and rights in the desert southwest. Under the Direction of Lynn Neuman, Artichoke Dance Company also annually produces an Eco-Arts Festival during NYC Climate Week on Governors Island, bringing visual and performing arts and climate consciousness together through participatory workshops, exhibitions, and performances. Neuman began Artichoke’s Immersive Performance Tours of Gowanus drawing on her many years of experience organizing with the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice. Artichoke’s ecoarts activism training program, Artichoke Ambassadors, and fellowship program, Arts Incubator for Change Making, trains and mentors the next generation of ecoarts activists. Incorporated as a non-profit in 1999, Artichoke Dance has held 23 New York seasons and toured nationally and internationally. For more info: www.artichokedance.org.

Event Description: Hop into a Gowanus Dredgers canoe and paddle at your own pace inside the protected Gowanus Canal. Enjoy discovering the canal’s unique mix of wildlife and urban waterway infrastructure, practice your paddling skills, or take a guided audio tour and learn more about the history, cleanup and revitalization of our favorite urban waterway. We’ll outfit you with a life jacket (which must be worn at all times) and paddle, offer some basic instruction on how to paddle and safety tips on how to use a canoe, and help you set off on your own self-guided journey. Trips may be limited to 20 minutes if there’s a crowd — but usually we just expect you to return to the dock 15 min. prior to closing. Who can participate? Paddling is for everyone! Free walk-up canoeing is open to all ages. Groups, families, solo paddlers, and intrepid first dates are all welcome! Minors require a guardian’s signature to participate, and all participants must sign a waiver. What should I wear? Dress for the weather: wear sunscreen, hats, and bring a water bottle — and bring layers if there’s a breeze! Close-toed shoes are recommended, and wear clothing you don’t mind potentially being splashed. Is it really free? Yes! But donations are encouraged to help us continue offering these and other programs. Can I volunteer? Yes! You can sign up to volunteer here. No prior experience is required, but we love return volunteers! Note: Volunteer shifts run from 30-minutes before the start of the program through the first two hours, or from the middle of the program to 30 minutes after the end of the scheduled time.

Event Name: Cultural Ecologies Series 2026: Unheard-of + Mehrnam Rastegari Trio
Event Description: Cultural Ecologies Series 2026: Unheard-of and the Gowanus Dredgers present Mehrnam Rastegari Trio Dredgers Bunker, 2 19th Street, NY 11232 Date and Time: September 19, 2026, 6:30PM Canoe Launch, 7PM Music On September 19th, Unheard-of presents a new expansive electroacoustic commission by Matt McBane exploring underwater topographies in acoustic and synth forms paired with a set by Mehrnam Rastegari and her trio. Rastegari is a prominent Persian musician, award-winning film score composer, and master Kamancheh player bringing Persian music in new directions with inflections of rock, jazz, and modern fusion. TICKET RSVP OR RESERVE YOUR CANOE SEAT HERE — These free performances will take place at the Gowanus Dredgers Bunker as well as their satellite locations including the paddle-in movie location and Boathouse (both ADA accessible). We are excited to expand our musical offerings with this new weekly jam. Dredger Host: Liz Rabson Schnore Jam Leader: Papa Ernie Vega What Jug band and String band music? Let’s start with String band music. Black String band music, which will be our focus, was created by Southern Blacks and pre-dates the Blues & Jazz. Groups which consisted of mostly stringed instruments (guitar, banjo, bass, violin, mandolin, ukulele, etc) performed a wide variety of songs and styles for all manner of social functions and for personal enjoyment; two-steps, waltzes and breakdowns for dances, ballads and love songs, humorous & novelty songs, as well as blues, jazz, and pop tunes as they came into fashion. This genre, sadly, was under-represented by the burgeoning recording industry in the 1920’s and 30’s, which helped contribute to its already declining popularity in the wake of the success of the Blues and Jazz: though groups like the Mississippi Sheiks and the Dallas String Band did make great and popular recordings. The genre never completely died out, however, and is alive and well today thanks to the perseverance of its practitioners and the dedication of its fans, which has led to a rediscovery and a new appreciation by audiences young and old. Jug band music developed in the early 20th century within Southern Black communities and was essentially a string band with a jug used as a “poor man’s tuba”, in the role of a bass instrument. Other household items as instruments were popular as well; washboard and/or spoons for percussion, washtub bass, and kazoo. These combined with the guitars, banjos, mandolins/violins of the traditional string band, along with the harmonica, made for a unique sound that won the hearts of the public in the early days of the recording industry. The Memphis Jug Band and Cannon’s Jug Stompers recorded well over a hundred examples of blues, ballads, pop and dance numbers – and they’re just the tip of the iceberg. The genre found new life in the Folk Music Revival of the 1960’s and remains popular to this day. These sessions will be open to Intermediate and above players, and we encourage you to sing along and bring a song to lead. To lead a song, you will be expected to sing it loudly enough for those around you to hear, to know the key you will sing in, and to explain the chord changes and form of the song if need be. We may also discuss some ideas for performing in an ensemble to help everyone find their place in the music. Papa Ernie Vega is a NYC singer, instrumentalist, bandleader, teacher, songwriter and performing/recording artist. He has over 20 years of professional experience and has performed at the Newport Folk Festival, the Jug Band Jubilee and the Osaka Jug Band Festival. He also taught and performed at the Port Townsend Acoustic Blues Festival from 2016-2021. He is a lover of fine cheap food, old movies, humor, and photography. Event Name: On Location with Artichoke Dance | Robin Michals
Event Description: On Location with Artichoke Dance is a solo exhibition by Brooklyn-based photographer Robin Michals. Curated by Pam Wong, the exhibit showcases photographs of Artichoke Dance Company performing the Immersive Performance Tours of Gowanus conceived by Lynn Neuman in 2021, and co-hosted annually with various environmental and social justice organizations. The photographs on view feature Artichoke dancers moving through Gowanus in space and time and include images at the defunct Salt Lot in 2021 and the new 420 Carroll Street development in 2026. Michals merges the genres of dance photography and urban landscape photography in vibrant shots that capture the performances as well as the evolution of the neighborhood. The photos juxtapose the dancers as they work together to create patterns and shapes against a backdrop of the transforming waterfront. The photos offer an interpretation of the performances as a positive vision of urban life that values art, collaboration, and environmental awareness. In addition, there is a portrait of Neuman, in costume, on the tipping floor at SIMS Municipal Recycling, taken for Michals and Neuman’s collaborative project Waste Side Story. Michals and Neuman met in 2018 through a residency offered by Works on Water and Underwater New York on Governors Island. Michals, who had been working on environmental issues for 15 years, was struck by Lynn’s upcycling of plastic bags into costumes, and the pair began to work together to make images of a dancer wearing the costumes at locations that reflect the lifecycle of plastics from production to various end points including landfills and oceans. Several of these images were exhibited at The Old Stone House in 2021. Robin shifted her focus to dance photography after the pandemic, starting with her work with the Times Square Project in 2020 and 2021. For Robin, photographing the Artichoke Dance tours is an incredible opportunity to bring together her longstanding love of urban landscape photography and her much more recent, but no less profound, love of dance photography. —————- ON LOCATION WITH ARTICHOKE DANCE On view Saturdays: Sept 12, 19, 26 and Oct 3 from 1-5pm ON LOCATION WITH ARTICHOKE DANCE Programs: Sept. 12 (2:00–2:30pm): Video screening of Immersive Performance Tour Highlights: 2021–2026 with Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 12 (2:30-4:30pm): Join a guided tour using the Gowanus Augmented Reality Walking Tour App featuring animated virtual environments of the past as visual overlays on the canal-scape, as well as the Underground Waterways Soundwalk where voices from the past murmur and sing, led by Sarah Drury, Project Director. iPads and headphones provided, or download to your iPhone. The 20-minute tour will be available from 2:30-4:30pm. Sept. 19 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 26 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company Sept. 26 (2:30pm): Role of the Arts in Change Making: A Conversation with Naturally Occurring Cultural Districts of New York Oct. 3 (2:00pm): Pop-up performance by Artichoke Dance Company —————- About the Artist: Robin Michals is a photographer who specializes in dance and performance. She is completely omnivorous when it comes to dance with an interest in all forms from folkloric to street dance. Her clients include the international Human Rights Arts Festival and the Queensboro Dance Festival among many others. In 2025, she had a public installation of photos of dancers at the party Vinyl Nights in Albee Square in Downtown Brooklyn, sponsored by Downtown Brooklyn Partnership. Her work has also been in numerous publications including Hyperallergic, Queens Chronicle, and Time Out. Before shifting her focus to performance, she spent 15 years documenting environment issues including climate change and the fossil fuel industries. She was raised in Manhattan and moved to Brooklyn in the last century. Robin has taught photography at City Tech, CUNY, where her students are from all over the world, for 23 years. For more info: www.robinmichals.com About Artichoke Dance: Artichoke Dance Company, based in Brooklyn, NY, is known for innovative and engaging performances paired with environmental activism, education, community building and civic engagement. Previous large-scale projects have addressed plastic pollution mitigation on Coney Island, single use plastic bags in New York, sea level rise and climate migration, the remediation of the Gowanus Canal, river revitalization in Los Angeles, and water use and rights in the desert southwest. Under the Direction of Lynn Neuman, Artichoke Dance Company also annually produces an Eco-Arts Festival during NYC Climate Week on Governors Island, bringing visual and performing arts and climate consciousness together through participatory workshops, exhibitions, and performances. Neuman began Artichoke’s Immersive Performance Tours of Gowanus drawing on her many years of experience organizing with the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice. Artichoke’s ecoarts activism training program, Artichoke Ambassadors, and fellowship program, Arts Incubator for Change Making, trains and mentors the next generation of ecoarts activists. Incorporated as a non-profit in 1999, Artichoke Dance has held 23 New York seasons and toured nationally and internationally. For more info: www.artichokedance.org.

Event Name: Brooklyn Folk Festival: Banjo Toss Competition
Event Description: Each year, as part of the Brooklyn Folk Festival , contestants gather on the banks of the fetid Gowanus Canal to see who can throw a banjo the farthest in the – BANJO TOSS: BANJO THROWING COMPETITION! The special “throwing banjo”, attached to a rope is tossed into the canal, a federally designate Super Fund site. The marked rope pays out, showing how far the banjo has been tossed. The Brooklyn Folk Festival is presented each year by the Jalopy Theatre & School of Music, a grassroots Red Hook, Brooklyn community space that is a music venue, music school, and record label. We are excited to support the Banjo Toss event activity so please stop by and join the fun! We are told the best preparation for this competition is to attend a show at the Brooklyn Folk Festival so purchase tickets now before they are sold out. While bearded men and women are growing in popularity as more people live, work and play in our Gowanus neighborhood, we are assured by the organizers that beards are optional. Our amazing collection of competitors reinforces the Dredgers theme of inclusion so stop by to cheer our competitors or compete in the toss as well!

Event Name: Exhibit: The Shirley Chisholm Way: Brooklyn's Blueprint for Change
Event Description: Join Prospect Park Alliance and Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) for a new exhibit that explores how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to fight for her community, becoming the first Black woman elected to Congress. The exhibit is organized around seven life lessons drawn from Chisholm’s tenacious career. It features stunning portraits of Chisholm by artist Al Johnson and rarely seen photographs and memorabilia from the Congresswoman’s campaigns, curated by Barbara Bullard, Creative Producer and President of SCCI. These materials offer inspirational insights into how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to become the first Black woman to serve in Congress. This exhibit provides visitors with a space to reflect on Chisholm’s legacy as Prospect Park Alliance welcomes the installation of a new monument in her honor at the Parkside and Ocean Avenue entrance in 2027. The exhibit, curated by Barbara Bullard, Cultural Producer and President of the Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute, is part of Prospect Park Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the museum to explore the legacies of resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family. SCCI is aligned with grassroots groups and frontline communities through creating substantive community-based partnership and collaboration along with strategic interoperative relationships with leaders of governmental, and mainstream organizations.

Event Name: Molière in the Park: Don Juan
Event Description: Join Molière in the Park, in partnership with Prospect Park Alliance, for a free production of Molière’s most subversive masterpiece, Don Juan. Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Here’s a chance to make an ongoing commitment to your community! Join a Prospect Park Alliance EcoZone Volunteer Crew to help Alliance gardeners care forBrooklyn’s Backyard! Prospect Park is divided into seven Ecological Zones (EcoZones) that are specifically maintained by dedicated EcoZone gardeners. We’re recruiting an EcoZone 2 Volunteer Crew to assist EcoZone Gardeners in restoration and general maintenance tasks to care for the zone that stretches along the Northeast side of the park from The Vale of Cashmere to Willink Plaza (Flatbush Avenue at Empire Boulevard), including the Midwood, from October 2026 to June 2027. Join us for an open house! Come out on a Wednesday in August and September, 9 am–12 pm to meet our Gardeners and get hands-on experience. Be advised, these projects involve repetitive bending, kneeling, lifting and transporting loaded wheelbarrows. This opportunity requires using sharp tools and encountering potentially hazardous plants and materials.
